events.reason: Itching, pale stools, dark urine, RUQ fullness

reports.text: Liver measures 18.5 cm in craniocaudal length, mildly enlarged, with normal echotexture and no focal lesion. Mild intrahepatic biliary prominence. Common bile duct dilated to 9 mm; distal duct obscured by bowel gas. Gallbladder contains multiple shadowing stones; wall normal thickness; no pericholecystic fluid; no sonographic tenderness. Pancreatic head poorly seen. Right kidney normal.
reports.conclusion: Cholelithiasis with dilated common bile duct, suggesting distal obstruction; MRCP recommended. Mild hepatomegaly.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department Physician Record
Date of visit: 12/23/2025
Sent by her primary physician.

HPI: 50-year-old woman with gallstones known since 2022 (failed ursodiol, declined surgery) and type 2 diabetes, here with two months of generalized itching, light-colored stools and dark urine, plus a sense of fullness in the right upper abdomen. She denies significant pain, fever, rigors or vomiting.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, obesity, hypothyroidism, chronic constipation, overactive bladder, rectal prolapse repaired 2024. PSH: laparoscopic rectopexy 2024.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, polyethylene glycol daily, multivitamin, ibuprofen PRN.
Allergies: NKDA. Social: no alcohol, never smoker.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable. Icteric skin and sclerae. Abdomen soft and nontender without masses; liver edge palpable, mildly enlarged.

Labs: total bilirubin 2.8, direct 1.9, alkaline phosphatase 420, AST 50, ALT 55. CBC, lipase, BMP and INR unremarkable.
Ultrasound: gallstones; CBD 9 mm; liver mildly enlarged.

MDM: cholestatic jaundice with dilated duct in a patient with gallstones, most likely choledocholithiasis; no signs of cholangitis. Malignant obstruction less likely but needs exclusion with MRCP.

Disposition: admitted to the hospitalist service with GI and surgery consultation.

reports.text: Specimen: gallbladder, laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Gross: gallbladder 7.5 x 3.0 cm, opened to reveal multiple yellow faceted stones up to 0.7 cm. Wall 0.2 cm. Microscopic: gallbladder wall with no dysplasia or malignancy. Cystic duct margin unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Gallbladder with cholesterol cholelithiasis. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: ERCP Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography
Date: 12/24/2025
Indication: obstructive jaundice; MRCP with distal common bile duct stone.
Sedation: general anesthesia.
Findings: normal major papilla. Deep biliary cannulation achieved. Cholangiogram: CBD dilated to about 10 mm with a 7 mm filling defect in the distal duct and smaller debris above it. Biliary sphincterotomy performed. Duct swept with an extraction balloon, removing one 7 mm stone and several fragments and sludge. Final occlusion cholangiogram showed no residual filling defects and good drainage. Pancreatic duct not injected.
Impression: choledocholithiasis, cleared.
Recommendation: cholecystectomy this admission; trend liver tests.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Hospital Discharge Summary
Admission 12/23/2025 - Discharge 12/27/2025

Principal diagnosis: obstructive jaundice due to choledocholithiasis.
Secondary: symptomatic cholelithiasis; type 2 diabetes; hypothyroidism.

Course:
Admitted from the ED with two months of pruritus, pale stools, dark urine and RUQ fullness, icteric with mild hepatomegaly. Bilirubin 2.8 (direct 1.9), alkaline phosphatase 420, AST 50, ALT 55. Ultrasound showed gallstones and a 9 mm CBD.
12/24: MRCP - 7 mm stone in the distal common bile duct, mild intrahepatic ductal dilation, multiple gallbladder stones, normal pancreas with no mass. ERCP the same afternoon with sphincterotomy and balloon clearance of the duct.
12/26: laparoscopic cholecystectomy by general surgery, uncomplicated. Previous rectopexy mesh noted in the pelvis, not disturbed. Bilirubin 1.6, alkaline phosphatase 310 that morning.
12/27: bilirubin 1.3, alkaline phosphatase 265, AST 34, ALT 41. Itching resolved, tolerating diet, pain controlled with acetaminophen.
Diabetes: metformin held around procedures, glucose 140-190 on a carbohydrate-controlled diet; metformin resumed 12/26 evening.
No antibiotics required (no cholangitis).

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily; multivitamin daily; acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed for incisional pain. Avoid ibuprofen for one week.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Pathology: gallbladder with cholesterol stones, no dysplasia or malignancy.
Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks with hepatic panel; general surgery in 4-6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call 2 days after discharge. Pt home, eating, mild soreness at incisions, acetaminophen twice a day. Itching gone, urine lighter. Meds reconciled with discharge summary. Appt 1/6 confirmed.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u. Admitted 12/23-12/27: obstructive jaundice from CBD stone, ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone clearance 12/24, lap chole 12/26. Path benign. Discharge summary and ERCP report reviewed.
Now: feels like herself. No itch, color back, stools brown, urine normal. Incisions sore only when she twists. Back to school next week. Using acetaminophen once a day, stopping soon. No fever.
Meds reconciled: metformin, levothyroxine, PEG, MVI; acetaminophen prn. Ibuprofen ok again now.
Exam: sclerae anicteric. Abd soft, laparoscopic incisions clean, mild tenderness at umbilical port. No hepatomegaly on my exam today.
A/P:
- Choledocholithiasis/cholelithiasis s/p ERCP and cholecystectomy: hepatic panel today. Jaundice resolved clinically.
- DM2: glucose ran a bit high inpatient, A1c due at March visit.
Surgery post-op visit early Feb.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bilirubin is normal again (0.8). Alkaline phosphatase is down from 420 to 132, nearly normal, and AST/ALT are normal. This is the expected recovery after the duct was cleared. We'll recheck with your physical.

documents.title: Postoperative Visit
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
General Surgery postoperative visit, 02/03/2026, about five weeks after laparoscopic cholecystectomy (following ERCP clearance of the bile duct).
She feels well, eating a normal diet without pain or diarrhea. No jaundice or itching. Bowels regular on polyethylene glycol; no prolapse symptoms.
Exam: incisions well healed, abdomen soft and nontender.
Pathology reviewed with her: gallstones, benign gallbladder.
Assessment: uneventful recovery. Discharged from surgical follow-up; return as needed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feeling good since the gallbladder came out. Surgeon released her in Feb. Eating smaller dinners now, a couple pounds down per our scale.
Bladder ok. Bowels regular.
Metformin 1000 BID, levo 100, PEG daily, MVI.
Exam: anicteric, abdomen benign, heart/lungs normal.
A1c and BMP today. Next: physical in August with full labs.

documents.title: A1c
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.7 - lowest in a few years. Nice work. Kidney function normal.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 51F, summer break so a morning slot.
Since last physical: Dec admission for CBD stone with jaundice, ERCP + lap chole, full recovery. Rectopexy 2024 holding. OAB stable, occasional urgency.
Eye exam booked for later this month.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, levothyroxine 100 mcg, polyethylene glycol 17 g daily, multivitamin, ibuprofen occasionally.
ROS negative.
Exam: well. Sclerae clear. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, healed port sites, NT. Breasts no masses. Feet: monofilament intact, DP/PT palpable, skin intact.
PHQ-9: 1.
Plan: CMP (including liver tests after the December episode), lipids, CBC, A1c, TSH, UACR. Mammogram due October. Flu and COVID at the fall clinic. Pap next 2030. Colonoscopy 2034.
DM follow-up mid-September.
